task: Stage 1 Workforce Identity: add explicit prepared-versus-enforced MFA activation control so the complete TOTP policy remains implemented but interactive workforce MFA stays parked until final audit activation, without changing RBAC, tenant authority, middleware, or parked PR #858.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The existing TOTP policy is security-sensitive and already implemented, but the active workforce login currently applies it immediately. The product-owner decision is to keep MFA prepared but non-blocking during ongoing visual/functional audit work and activate enforcement only near final audit. This transaction must separate policy truth from activation state without weakening the target policy or activating parked server-side AAL2 enforcement.

acceptanceCriteria: The canonical target TOTP policy remains unchanged: platform owner requires two factors, platform admin one, store owner/admin one, sensitive operations one, low-risk roles zero.
A canonical prepared/enforced activation mode is introduced under DOMAIN-IDENTITY without creating a second authentication authority.
Prepared mode is the default when no explicit activation value is configured and produces an effective interactive workforce TOTP requirement of zero while preserving the target policy value.
Enforced mode produces the effective TOTP requirement from the unchanged target policy.
The workforce-context route returns both effective and policy TOTP requirements plus the activation mode from server-owned configuration.
The canonical workforce login therefore remains usable for current visual/functional audits without mandatory TOTP enrollment/challenge while the activation mode is prepared.
No role, tenant, middleware authorization authority or parked PR #858 server-side AAL2 enforcement is added, weakened, merged or activated.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only session/password/MFA authority.
requiredWorkforceTotpFactors remains the canonical Market Ready target-policy function and retains existing owner/admin semantics.
Activation state changes only the effective interactive login requirement; it does not alter role membership, tenant resolution or authorization decisions.
Unknown or absent activation configuration resolves to prepared, never silently to enforced.
Final enforcement requires an explicit future activation transaction; this release does not claim Market Ready AAL2 enforcement.
The active delegator PR #912 remains separate and is not merged or modified by this Auth Core transaction.

failureModes: The implementation changes owner/admin target factor counts to zero instead of separating policy from activation.
A missing environment value accidentally enables MFA and makes every visual audit require TOTP.
A client-visible/public environment flag becomes the authority for security activation.
Prepared mode suppresses the target policy value entirely, making final activation unverifiable or easy to forget.
The workforce-context route continues returning the raw target policy as the effective login requirement and still blocks the E13/visual audit login flow.
The fix edits requireAdmin, middleware, tenant resolution or PR #858 and prematurely activates server enforcement.
The activation correction is mixed into PR #912 and recreates the high-risk mixed-release budget failure.
edgeCases: Undefined, empty, whitespace and unknown activation values resolve to prepared.
Only the exact canonical enforced value activates the target policy.
Prepared owner context reports policyRequiredFactors=2 but requiredFactors=0.
Prepared admin context reports policyRequiredFactors=1 but requiredFactors=0.
Enforced owner/admin contexts report effective values identical to the target policy.
Low-risk operator remains zero in both prepared and enforced modes.
Existing verified TOTP factors remain untouched in Supabase; prepared mode does not unenroll or mutate them.

alternatives.summary: Change requiredWorkforceTotpFactors so owner/admin temporarily return zero.
alternatives.reason: That destroys the canonical Market Ready policy and conflates target security requirements with activation timing.

alternatives.summary: Teach E13/visual proof tooling to bypass the workforce MFA state machine.
alternatives.reason: That would hide a real product activation mismatch and create special test authentication semantics.

alternatives.summary: Activate PR #858 and force full AAL2 now.
alternatives.reason: This contradicts the accepted audit workflow and would make routine visual/functional audit access unnecessarily burdensome.

alternatives.summary: Preserve target policy but derive the effective login requirement from an explicit server-owned prepared/enforced activation mode.
alternatives.reason: This keeps the complete security design implemented and testable while honoring the deliberate activation timing boundary.

specialistReviews.finding: Defaulting owner/admin target policy itself to zero would weaken security truth.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep requiredWorkforceTotpFactors unchanged; introduce a separate effective activation calculation with target policy still observable.

specialistReviews.finding: MFA activation belongs to DOMAIN-IDENTITY and must not be owned by preview, storefront, middleware or quality harness code.
specialistReviews.resolution: Only auth policy/context plus neutral regressions are editable; #912 delegates consume the resulting canonical contract later.

specialistReviews.finding: Mixing the activation correction into the ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegator release would reopen the release-risk problem.
specialistReviews.resolution: Ship this as an isolated Auth Core transaction first; reconstruct #912 from verified main afterward.

challenge.scenario: WORKFORCE_MFA_MODE is unset during current audits.
challenge.finding: Raw target policy would force owner/admin enrollment or challenge immediately.
challenge.resolution: Canonical mode resolver returns prepared and effective requiredFactors=0.

challenge.scenario: A typo or unknown activation value is deployed.
challenge.finding: Silently treating unknown input as enforced would unexpectedly lock audit users behind MFA.
challenge.resolution: Only exact enforced activates; all other values resolve to prepared in this pre-final-audit release.

challenge.scenario: A developer solves the audit problem by changing owner/admin target factor counts.
challenge.finding: Market Ready security policy truth would be lost.
challenge.resolution: Regression tests keep owner=2/admin=1 and test activation separately.

challenge.scenario: Prepared mode hides the future required factor count.
challenge.finding: The system could appear to have no MFA policy and final activation could overclaim readiness.
challenge.resolution: Context exposes both policyRequiredFactors and effective requiredFactors plus mfaMode.

challenge.scenario: The E13 proof account is owner/admin.
challenge.finding: Canonical login currently stops on TOTP before E13 proof, proving activation is already operationally enforced.
challenge.resolution: Prepared mode lets canonical password/context flow complete without test-only bypass; E13 can then prove the real engine.

challenge.scenario: The correction edits requireAdmin/middleware or merges #858.
challenge.finding: Server-side AAL2 authorization enforcement would become active before the planned final audit.
challenge.resolution: Those authorities remain impacted-read-only and dedicated regressions retain the parked boundary.

challenge.scenario: The correction is committed directly into #912.
challenge.finding: High-risk auth and three non-auth subsystems would again become one mixed release.
challenge.resolution: Use an isolated Auth Core branch and merge to main before reconstructing #912.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the exact plan-only head before implementation.
Add pure prepared/enforced activation semantics while preserving requiredWorkforceTotpFactors target-policy behavior.
Update workforce-context to derive effective factors server-side and expose target/effective/mode evidence.
Add deterministic policy/activation/source-contract regressions, including no parked AAL2 enforcement.
Run Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Known Failure Replay.
Require Release Risk Budget PASS for the isolated Auth Core transaction.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before merge to main; only then reconstruct #912.

requirements.requirement: Workforce MFA keeps the canonical Market Ready target policy fully implemented while an explicit server-owned prepared/enforced activation mode controls the effective interactive login requirement; current default remains prepared until final audit.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Owner/admin target TOTP policy must remain 2/1 and must not be reduced to solve activation timing.
Absent or non-enforced activation configuration must not force TOTP during current audit workflows.
MFA activation must remain server-owned and must not be delegated to client/public configuration.
This release must not activate requireAdmin/middleware AAL2 enforcement or merge parked PR #858.

requirements.requirement: The high-risk MFA activation-control change ships as an isolated auth release within the canonical Release Risk Budget and does not mix with #912 delegator changes.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The activation-control release must not contain substantive ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegator changes or recreate the original mixed release.

notes: Live exact-head E13 proof on PR #912 exposed an activation mismatch: canonical workforce login correctly follows requiredWorkforceTotpFactors, so the current owner/admin proof account is stopped by TOTP before E13 can run. This is not an E13 defect and must not be hidden by a quality-harness bypass. Product-owner direction remains: MFA/AAL2 is implemented now but enforcement is activated only near final audit. This isolated Auth Core correction separates target policy from activation state. PR #912 remains DRAFT and will be reconstructed from the new verified main; PR #858 remains parked.
